title: Ontario permit-to-start-to-completion conversion evidence
question: Which permit intentions become starts, completions, and occupancy?
why_it_matters: Building permits are upstream intentions. FTFN needs conversion evidence to know whether approvals become starts, completions, occupied units, or stalled projects.
current_support: FTFN has Statistics Canada permits, CMHC starts and completions data, a June 2026 CMHC Toronto CMA baseline separating approved units awaiting starts, units under construction, completions, and starts, Toronto's 2025 Development Pipeline, application 24 254930 records through City Council adoption on July 29-30, 2026, and a bounded full-address Building Permit portal recheck.
missing_evidence: building permit and permit-to-start conversion for application 24 254930
candidate_records: specific Toronto building permit for application 24 254930
application 24 254930 start, completion, and occupancy record
next_action: Keep CMHC's metropolitan stage stocks and flows separate and do not calculate an unmatched conversion rate. Recheck the bill and condition trail on September 9, then search the Building Permit portal using a confirmed application or later project identifier and track construction start, completion, and occupancy.

named_records: City of Toronto Building Application Status portal
Toronto City Council item 2026.SC33.9 for application 24 254930
latest_review.stage_result: The selected application has a verified Council disposition but remains upstream of enacted amendments, a confirmed building permit, construction start, completion, and occupancy. The aggregate baseline still supplies no matched project cohort.
latest_review.stop_rule: Do not divide approved-not-started stock by monthly starts or completions, infer a project permit from an address search, or treat Council adoption as a permit or delivered unit.

notes: Phase 61 reconciles the completed Council decision and retains the project boundary. The earlier eight address searches returned Application Not Found, but those bounded negative queries do not prove that no permit exists.
